# PERICARDITIS

Most cases arise from non-infectious causes or are associated with viruses.

Antimicrobial therapy is not indicated unless pericardial fluid is purulent. If fluid is purulent, pericardial drainage is required in most cases. Modify antimicrobial regimen and narrow coverage based on results of culture and susceptibility tests.

Cardiology consultation is essential for management of therapy. Infectious Diseases consultation is recommended if an infectious origin is suspected.

# Duration of therapy

Duration is based on patient specific factors such as resolution of fever and clinical signs of infection. Generally, duration is 2 to 4 weeks depending on how adequacy of drainage of pericardial fluid and susceptibility of infectious organism.
